mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility service provider or regulated bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the South African incorporation agent and registered office representative

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the corporate shareholder or proposed funding bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, project counterparties and material sub-contractors against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) List, Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) targeted financial sanctions list under POCDATARA, and Interpol Red Notices; statutory enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs and domestic prominent influential persons (DPIPs) in accordance with FIC public compliance guidance and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services / bizeService portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be registered in any of South Africa's official languages provided it is capable of being rendered in the Roman alphabet; names containing non-Roman script must be transliterated; the name must not be offensive, undesirable, misleading, imply state patronage, or be confusingly similar to an existing company name or registered trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC rejection of a proposed name under sections 12 or 16 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, the applicant may request written reasons and lodge an application to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 for a binding determination; alternatively, the applicant may re-submit the same or an amended name once the CIPC objection has been cured, paying a fresh reservation fee; any residual administrative decision may be reviewed by the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the serviced or virtual office supplies a physical South African street address for service of process and statutory correspondence; a post office box is not acceptable. For a hyperscale data center electromechanical EPC contractor, a pure virtual office may be treated as elevated risk by FICA accountable institutions and project lenders; a physical project-site office plus registered head office is the commercial norm.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-moderate (approximately 15% annualized) risk of unannounced CIPC or SARS inspection at the registered office; significantly higher (approximately 60% annualized) risk of unannounced on-site occupational health and safety, COIDA and construction compliance inspections by the Department of Employment and Labour and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) at project sites.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13(1), 14, 15, 19 and 40; Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1), together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no required escrow/allowance account. A Pty Ltd may issue one or more shares for cash or in-kind consideration. Directors must ensure shares are issued for adequate consideration under s 40 before allotment; subscribers may pay consideration directly to the company after incorporation or as agreed in the share subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers' shares set out in the Memorandum of Incorporation be allotted and issued to Ms. Nomvula Khumalo and Mr. Pieter van der Merwe. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be 15 Riebeeck Street, Cape Town, and that such address be the company's domicilium citandi et executandi. FURTHER RESOLVED that Mr. Pieter van der Merwe be appointed Managing Director, Ms. Nomvula Khumalo Financial Director, and Mr. Thabo Mokoena Company Secretary, with authority to exercise powers under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the MOI. The officers are instructed to complete CIPC and SARS registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the CIPC company name register to confirm availability, then submit Form CoR 9.1 for reservation of a primary name and up to four alternative names in order of preference. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee and retain the transaction receipt.
required_dossiers: Proposed primary name and alternative names
Certified ID or passport copies of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC refuses the name as confusingly similar, offensive, or already registered, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with a different distinguishing element or request CIPC reconsideration within the period stated in the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the MOI and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices for lodgement; incorporators sign the MOI and Notice offline or electronically
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI using the CIPC model MOI or a custom MOI compliant with the Companies Act. Each incorporator must sign the MOI and complete CoR 14.1, including director and officer consents. Initial every page and attach certified foreign identity documents where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified ID or passport copies of all incorporators
Written consent of each named director and officer to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries signature, consent, or attachment defects, resubmit corrected signed pages through the CIPC case management system within 10 business days or the application will be treated as abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge the incorporation application with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices (www.cipc.co.za) or an accredited CIPC branch office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC eServices, register the company transaction, upload the signed MOI and CoR 14.1 in PDF, verify the company details, pay the prescribed incorporation fee, and retain the CIPC transaction number for tracking.
required_dossiers: MOI and CoR 14.1 in accepted electronic format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any CIPC letter of query or defect via the eServices case portal within the prescribed deadline, amend the submitted documents as requested, and resubmit; failure to respond timely may require a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the registration certificate and company number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After CIPC approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from eServices. Verify the company name, registration number, date of incorporation, and limited liability status. Request a certified company register extract if required by banks or tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, file an application for rectification with CIPC together with the evidence of the correct data; CIPC will issue a corrected certificate once the application is approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), via eFiling or a SARS branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the SARS business registration process as soon as the company is registered. Register for Income Tax, VAT where the taxable turnover threshold is or will be exceeded, PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy where the company is an employer. Submit the company bank account details and board-approved address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS raises a verification query or requests additional information, attend a verification interview or submit the requested records via eFiling within the time limit; obtain or update the Tax Compliance Status pin once the registration is finalised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as an employer with the Compensation Fund and UIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL), Compensation Fund and Unemployment Insurance Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Compensation Fund for COIDA coverage and with the Unemployment Insurance Fund for employee benefits. Submit the employer registration forms, employee details, and declaration of earnings. Obtain the employer registration number before hiring workers on site.
required_dossiers: Directors' and employees' personal identity documents
Bank account details for fund payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DEL records the wrong industry classification, submit a written objection and the corrected activity description for ISIC 4100 datacenter EPC work; the registration record is then amended within 5 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) acting under the Construction Industry Development Board Act 38 of 2000
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CIDB Contractor Registration Certificate (Certificate of Registration as a Contractor)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and the competent provincial environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment under Listing Notices 1 and 3 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 where datacenter electrical infrastructure, diesel generators, substations, or substantial earthmoving exceed the applicable thresholds. A full Scoping and Environmental Impact Assessment may be required in sensitive environments or where high-voltage transmission infrastructure is part of the EPC scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cooling-water and wastewater discharges must comply with the National Water Act 36 of 1998, either under a General Authorisation or a water use licence. Air emissions from standby generators must meet the Minimum Emission Standards under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 where listed. VOC, refrigerant, hazardous waste, and thermal discharge limits are set in the environmental authorisation or applicable exemption, and asbestos or hazardous waste must be handled by registered transporters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval and fire protection system certification under the National Building Regulations and SANS 10400-3; structural load inspections for raised floors, plant decks, and cooling towers by a registered professional engineer; occupational clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including an Electrical Installation Certificate of Compliance and a municipal Certificate of Occupancy before operational use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), 299 Bronkhorst Street, Nieuw Muckleneuk, Pretoria; official portal and eFiling platform at https://efiling.sars.gov.za; customs administration through the SARS Customs Division (SAD500 declaration system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a locally incorporated (Pty) Ltd, CIPC transmits incorporation data to SARS and SARS issues an income tax reference number (TIN) upon registration; the company must maintain active eFiling credentials and notify SARS of registered address and director changes. A foreign entity deriving South African-source income (e.g., through a permanent establishment for EPC works) must apply for a SARS income tax reference number using the prescribed SARS Registration (RA) forms via eFiling or a SARS branch office. VAT registration: compulsory registration is required within 21 days after the end of the month in which taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in a rolling 12-month period or are reasonably expected to exceed that threshold; voluntary registration is available once turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000; foreign suppliers of electronic services must register where electronic services supplied to South African recipients exceed ZAR 50,000 in any 12-month period. The entity receives a distinct VAT registration number (10 digits, normally commencing with 4). A SARS Customs client code must also be obtained before lodging import or export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a resident (Pty) Ltd is a separate taxable person subject to corporate income tax at 27% on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment is available; distributions to shareholders are subject to dividends tax at 20%; non-resident companies are taxed only on South African-source income (territorial nexus).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in South Africa; classification follows the entity's legal form. Available statutory elections include: (i) Headquarter Company election under s 9I of the Income Tax Act (ITA) for qualifying companies with foreign shareholders or foreign operations; (ii) intra-group restructuring rollover elections under s 45 ITA (asset-for-share and share-for-share) subject to anti-avoidance conditions; (iii) VAT group election under s 50 of the VAT Act allowing connected companies to be registered as a single VAT group; (iv) controlled foreign company (CFC) elections under s 9D ITA, including the high-taxed exclusion; and (v) hybrid mismatch rules operative from 1 January 2020 under the ITA, which automatically deny deductions or include income in hybrid mismatch arrangements and cannot be neutralised by taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in a rolling 12-month period (actual or reasonably expected); voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 turnover; foreign electronic services suppliers: ZAR 50,000 of electronic services supplied to South African recipients.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not operate real-time fiscal pre-clearance or digital stamping. SARS mandates electronic filing via eFiling and has issued the binding Standard for Electronic Invoicing (SEI), with voluntary early adoption preceding a phased mandatory application from 1 January 2026. SEI requires structured, machine-readable electronic tax invoices in compliant XML formats (UBL/CII), issuance through SARS-compliant software, five-year electronic archiving, and machine-to-machine/API transmission capability. No government clearance token is affixed, but every tax invoice must contain the vendor VAT number, invoice number, supply date, description, value of supply, and VAT amount to support input deductions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to non-residents qualify for zero-rating under s 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, provided the goods are physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of the tax invoice date and the vendor retains prescribed proof of export. Cross-border services supplied to non-residents qualify under s 11(2)(l) where the recipient is outside South Africa at the time of supply, the services are not supplied directly in connection with South African land or improvements, are not supplied in connection with movable property remaining in South Africa, and are not used or enjoyed in South Africa. Datacenter electromechanical EPC services performed at a South African site are standard-rated at 15% due to the land nexus; services performed for a foreign data-center site may qualify for zero-rating. Imported subcontracted services are subject to reverse-charge VAT under ss 7(1)(c) and 54. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated export supplies is refundable under s 44(4) of the VAT Act, with prescribed interest if SARS fails to pay the refund within 21 business days.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank-validated payment confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS e-audit and risk-flagging algorithms scrutinise export declarations, bill-of-lading dates, proof of receipt and forex circularity. Failure to substantiate zero-rating within the required period triggers additional VAT at 15%, interest under the Tax Administration Act (TAA), and understatement penalties up to 200% of the shortfall in egregious cases (s 223 TAA), with criminal prosecution for deliberate fraudulent zero-rating. Refund claims may be suspended during verification; assessments can be reopened retrospectively within the TAA prescription framework, extended in non-disclosure cases and unlimited in cases of fraud or misrepresentation; false export documentation also attracts administrative penalties, forfeiture and perjury-based sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), the delegated Exchange Control authority for the Republic of South Africa
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is convertible on the current account without prior SARB approval for genuine trade and service transactions, provided that supporting documentation is retained by an Authorised Dealer. Capital account transactions remain subject to exchange control approval thresholds and require engagement via Authorised Dealers or FinSurv for securities, loans, FDI, and certain holdings. Dividend and profit remittances to non-residents are permitted on production of an audited certificate or independent accountant verification that the dividends are declared out of distributable reserves and after satisfaction of the applicable dividends tax under the Income Tax Act. Practical hurdles include timely AML/KYC clearance, notification of large transactions through the Cross-Border Electronic Reporting system, and compliance with the 180-day repatriation timeline for trade proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment unless an extension is granted by an Authorised Dealer. There is no fixed statutory mandatory conversion percentage into ZAR; however, the proceeds must be surrendered to an Authorised Dealer or credited to an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) in accordance with the SARB Exchange Control Manual. Funds held in an FCA may only be used for permissible trade and financial transactions and must be repatriated and converted if directed by FinSurv. The exporter must submit a Bill of Entry and proof of receipt to the bank within the prescribed period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
First National Bank (FNB) – FirstRand Bank Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs). Such EMIs are not licensed as South African banks and may not provide domestic current account services, but they can support auxiliary payment routing for cross-border disbursements if the primary liquidity remains with a SARB-authorised dealer bank. Use of a non-licensed EMI as the sole treasury conduit is legally constrained due to exchange control requirements. EMIs must be jurisdictionally licensed, must not hold ZAR-denominated balances on behalf of the South African entity in a manner constituting unauthorized banking, and must provide full transaction audit trails for exchange control verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one natural person director or an authorised senior officer of the (Pty) Ltd entity must physically appear before the relationship banker at a branch office or at a notary public for FICA onboarding. Most Tier-1 banks now accept a hybrid process: remote digital biometric verification for the majority of directors, provided that a physical in-country representative (e.g., a registered director or a PoA holder) is available for a structured compliance interview. Foreign directors not physically present must provide notarially attested and apostilled identification and proof of address documents; the bank may impose enhanced due diligence for non-resident ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: ultimate shareholders sitting in a multi-jurisdictional holding chain with low-tax-privilege entities or registered agents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete, certified corporate organogram from the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) down to the South African (Pty) Ltd, accompanied by share registers, register of members, trust deeds or declaration of trust, notarised passports of all natural UBOs, and a written explanation of the commercial value chain for the data centre EPC business. Where nominee shareholders are used, provide formal nominee declarations and written acknowledgment of the underlying principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch: inbound equity capital or shareholder loan exceeding average sector turnover and inconsistent with available financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury and funding memorandum containing the full capital injection timeline, executed shareholder loan agreements or subscription agreements, company audited or independently reviewed financial statements for the last two years, bank statements from the originating foreign bank account showing the sustainability of accumulated funds, foreign tax returns or proof of legitimate commercial earnings, and forecast annual cash flows for the hyperscale data centre EPC contract. Where funds originate from a third-party lender, include the facility agreement, security documents, and evidence of lender licensing and credit approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value EPC trade counterparty risk: large advance payments to foreign equipment suppliers located in higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full procurement dossier for each major outbound disbursement containing the signed commercial contract, pro-forma invoices, HS codes, Incoterms, certificate of origin, export/import permits, equipment specifications, and a risk-based assessment of the supplier bank and jurisdiction. Provide insurance or guarantees where applicable (e.g., advance payment bond, performance guarantee) and correspondence evidencing the genuine arm's-length nature of the transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder loan injections must be channelled through a SARB-authorised dealer bank using designated cross-border wire protocols (SWIFT MT103 cover or MT202, depending on currency) and the correct purpose codes for foreign direct investment (e.g., code 500 FDI equity) or shareholder loans (code 501/510). The bank will require a foreign investment declaration, identity of the immediate and ultimate investor, share subscription documents (for equity), and loan agreements for debt funding. For amounts above the SARB reporting threshold, Form FDI or an electronic reporting through the Currency and Exchanges Manual will be triggered. Prior FinSurv approval may be required for certain inward capital structures involving financial assistance (e.g., loans from non-resident shareholders under section 45 of the Companies Act combined with exchange control rules).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the EPC works are cleared through SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or via Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700 series) opened through a South African Authorised Dealer. For foreign suppliers requiring documentary security, a confirmed, irrevocable L/C issued by an international bank and advised through a South African authorised dealer is the preferred clearing rail. For domestic subcontractor payments in ZAR, utilise the local real-time gross settlement system (SAMOS) and Electronic Funds Transfer rails. All trade-related payments must be supported by appropriate customs declarations, supplier invoices, and transport documents to satisfy exchange control audit and SARB reporting. Any advance payment above the prescribed threshold must be evidenced by bank guarantees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts with an Authorised Dealer
Forward exchange contracts (through a South African Authorised Dealer) to hedge committed future USD, EUR, GBP exposures
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts, permissible only where underlying non-resident counterparty structure is proven and the transaction is entered into with a local authorised dealer
Cross-currency swaps for hedging capital and interest flows on foreign-currency-denominated borrowings
Currency options where permitted by the bank's risk appetite and subject to FinSurv reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 business days after the company's incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of ZAR 100 per month (approx USD 6) or a maximum administrative penalty of ZAR 5,000; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in compulsory deregistration (strike-off) by CIPC under section 82(4) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (included in CoR 36.1 annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Properties Commission (CIPC) - Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same filing window as the annual return; within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit accurate beneficial ownership particulars is an offence under Regulation 37 of the Companies Act, punishable by a fine up to ZAR 200,000 (approx USD 11,800) and/or imprisonment not exceeding 10 years, in addition to annual late-penalty exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual B-BBEE Compliance Report under section 13G of the B-BBEE Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: B-BBEE Commission (oversight authority under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the date of approval of the audited financial statements; for entities with a 31 March year-end, the statutory submission season closes on 30 June following the year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission by a qualifying measured entity constitutes an offence; the Commission may impose an administrative fine of not more than 10% of annual turnover and commence civil enforcement under section 13G(3).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company's public interest score (calculated under Regulation 26 of the Companies Act) equals or exceeds 350; audit is also required for a non-public company whose PIS is 100-349 if financial statements were compiled internally (or if any controlling entity or member requires it); public companies and state-owned companies controlled by a public company are always audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by IASB, with IFRS for SMEs permitted for companies not required to use full IFRS and below the turnover thresholds set out in the Companies Act disclosure regulations; local South African GAAP is no longer a separate mainstream framework for for-profit entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Within each annual return cycle, the board must submit a declaration of all beneficial ownership transfers effected since the last confirmation. A share transfer in the securities register must be reported to CIPC through the annual return; any new beneficial owner or change in ownership percentage must be reflected in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register and filed with CIPC within 14 days of the transfer or the director becoming aware.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200–$500 per annum for a registered office service; $150–$350 for a nominee agent business address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $6,500–$18,000 per annum for a statutory audit of an EPC contractor with significant construction contracts

stage_6.entry_description: Registration particulars: legal name, registration number, tax reference number, financial year end.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not described on ITR14; beneficial ownership of shares is separately reported for dividend tax via the DTD declaration to the payer.
